minor.issue: The placeholder detector does a case-insensitive substring scan on the raw HTML for the literal word 'placeholder' (among others). This will false-positive on any legitimate AI output that uses the English word — e.g. CSS class names like `class='placeholder-img'`, alt text like `alt='placeholder for cover image'`, or even Arabic sentences containing the loanword. Recommend tightening to word-boundary matches against the visible text-only payload (`_text_only`) rather than the full HTML, mirroring what `audit_html` already does.

action_items: (MINOR) Tighten mark_page_built placeholder detector — match against text-only payload with word boundaries instead of full HTML substring, otherwise legitimate pages that happen to contain the loanword 'placeholder' (CSS classes, alt text, marketing copy) will be falsely flagged as incomplete and blocked from being marked built.

(OBSERVABILITY) Add a logger.info / metrics counter when _strip_scaffold_placeholders actually removes content at serve time — right now we can't measure how often the AI is leaving scaffold text behind in production, which is the exact failure mode the user has been chasing for 72+ hours.
critical_code_review_comments: freebuild_chat.py crossed 7000 lines this iteration. The file mixes router setup, ~10 utility helpers (_strip_scaffold_placeholders, _inject_zenrex_footer, _inject_base_href, _splice_before_body_close, etc.), and the full agent-chat-stream lifecycle including the new lab branch. Lab-mode code (lines ~6680-6735) is conceptually a separate flow and would be much more testable if extracted into a dedicated `lab_chat.py` module that accepts (proj, message, history, ctx_holder) and returns an async generator. Right now there's no way to unit-test the lab branch end-to-end without standing up the full FastAPI app + DB + JWT chain.

The lab-mode branch silently force-sets workflow_state.stage='surgical_edit' on the in-memory copy (line 6688). This is fine because it's a copy, BUT the comment 'most permissive — no addendum constraints' is a brittle promise: if a future workflow stage adds new tool gates, the lab will inherit them. Consider passing an explicit `bypass_workflow_gates=True` flag to stream_agent_turn instead of piggy-backing on the 'surgical_edit' stage as a backdoor.

mark_page_built's placeholder matcher uses `p.lower() in page_html.lower()` which calls `.lower()` on the entire HTML string per placeholder (10 strings × full-page-HTML scan = O(N×K)). For a 100kB page this is ~1MB of string work per call. Cheap to call once but worth caching `page_html.lower()` outside the loop. Same anti-pattern exists in audit_html.

_strip_scaffold_placeholders builds 4 regex compilations on every call (line 250-271). With per-page-view publication serving, this is hot enough to be worth pre-compiling at module load. Not urgent but trivial to fix.

freebuild_agent.py is at 10.5k lines (was 10.7k iter65). The mark_page_built handler (~80 lines), the write_full_html incomplete_warning addition, and the create_page scaffold template would all be cleaner in a dedicated multi_page_tools.py sub-module.

rca_of_the_issue:
ROOT CAUSE of the 72-hour 'AI builds page 1, leaves pages 2-4 blank' user complaint: the create_page tool was inserting a literal `

محتوى الصفحة قيد البناء...

` scaffold paragraph into every newly created page. The AI would then add real sections via apply_section (so the page actually had 7-10k chars of real HTML as DB inspection confirmed) but FORGET to remove the scaffold paragraph. End users saw the Arabic 'قيد البناء' text dominating the visual top of every non-homepage and assumed the page was empty. THIS ITERATION's fix: (a) create_page template now emits only an HTML *comment* `` — no visible text in the body; (b) _strip_scaffold_placeholders runs at serve time on both /s/{slug} and /s/{slug}/{filename} as a belt-and-suspenders cleanup for sites built before this fix; (c) mark_page_built now refuses to flag a page 'built' until it has ≥2 sections AND ≥600 chars of real text AND no banned placeholder strings — which forces the AI to keep iterating with write_full_html until the page is genuinely populated. The new Lab Mode is the user's A/B-test tool to confirm whether the remaining failure modes (if any) live in the Brain orchestrator layer (Lab bypasses it) or in the underlying Claude/GPT/GLM models (Lab uses them directly with identical tools). All three fixes verified by tests in this iteration; the live SSE round-trip was dispatched but not awaited to completion in the smoke test to avoid burning credits.
